en: Petavatthu,
Mahāvagga 4.
The Story of the Female Ghost Revatī
“Arise, Revatī, you of most evil character!
You who keep your doors open and have no habit of giving!
We shall lead you away to where those who fare ill are sung of.”
"The denizens of hell are overwhelmed by suffering.
Having spoken thus, those two great yakṣas with blood-red eyes were Yama’s messengers.
Taking Revata by his arms,
they brought him before the host of gods, [saying]:
"He is of sun-like color, beautiful and radiant."
Whose is this celestial mansion, auspicious and covered with a golden lattice,
filled with people and shining like the rays of the sun?
Multitudes of women, anointed with the essence of sandalwood,
adorn the celestial mansion on both sides;
it appears with a radiance equal to the sun.
“Who rejoices, having reached heaven in a celestial mansion?
“In Bārāṇasī there was one named Nandiya,
a lay follower, free from stinginess, a master of giving, and generous.”
That celestial mansion,
crowded with people and shining like the rays of the sun,
was filled with throngs of women anointed with the essence of sandalwood.
They adorn the celestial mansion on both sides;
it appears with a color equal to the sun,
and having reached heaven, he rejoices in that mansion.
“I am Nandiya’s wife, a householder,
the mistress of the entire household;
I shall delight in my husband’s celestial mansion, and I shall give gifts.”
“Do not long for the sight of hell.
“This is your hell, O you of evil nature;
no merit has been performed by you in the world of the living.”
"For one who is stingy, irascible,
and of evil character does not attain companionship with those who go to heaven.
"What indeed is this excrement and urine?"
It appears impure;
what is this foul-smelling filth,
and what is it that exudes from it?
“This is indeed the Saṃsāvaka,
profound and worthy of the sages;
wherein for thousands of years— ”
“You are being roasted, Revatī.
“What evil deed have I done with body, speech, or mind?”
“By whom was this companion obtained,
so profound and a man of a hundred virtues?
“Both among recluses and brahmins...”
Or even other seekers after gain;
you deceived them with false speech—
this evil was committed by you.
By that, he obtained a dwelling,
deep and a hundred fathoms high;
there, for thousands of years,
You are cooked, Revatī!
They cut off even your hands, and then your feet;
they cut off even your ears, and then your nose.
Then flocks of ravens and owls,
having gathered and come together, devour me as I writhe.
"It would be well indeed if you would lead me back."
I shall perform much wholesome merit:
through giving, through even conduct,
and through restraint and self-control.
“Having done which they become happy and do not later regret it.
“Having previously been negligent, you— ”
Now you lament;
you shall experience the ripening of the deeds you yourself have done.
“Who, having gone from the world of the gods to the world of men,
might say this to me when asked:
‘Give gifts to those who have laid down the rod;’”
“Clothing, bedding, food, and drink— indeed,
one who is stingy, irascible, and of evil character does not attain companionship with those who have gone to heaven.”
Having surely gone from here and obtained a human birth,
may I be generous and endowed with virtue.
I shall perform much wholesome merit through generosity, righteous conduct,
self-restraint, and self-mastery.
I shall plant groves and causeways on difficult paths,
as well as ponds and wells.
With a serene mind,
on the fourteenth and the fifteenth,
and on the eighth day of the fortnight.
And during the fortnight of miracles,
I shall observe the Uposatha day, perfectly endowed with its eight factors.
Always restrained in virtuous conduct,
I shall not be negligent in giving;
this has been seen by me for myself.
While she was thus lamenting and writhing here and there,
they hurled her into a terrible hell.
With feet upturned and head hanging down:
"In the past, I was miserly and used to revile ascetics and brahmins."
"And having deceived my husband with falsehood,
I am now burning in a hell of terrible form.
The Story of the Petī Revatī, the Fourth.
